items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 and partners-only Mythos 5
items.diff_narrative: This is a net-new launch with no 2026-06-09 antecedent. Anthropic made its Mythos-class frontier model generally available as Claude Fable 5 - a safety-routed public release reporting 95.0% on SWE-bench Verified versus Opus 4.8's 88.6% - alongside an unrestricted partners-only twin, Mythos 5. The standout shift versus yesterday is the architecture itself: rather than a single uniform public frontier model, the day introduces a tiered split (a routed, terms-enforced public model plus an unrestricted partner model) and a disclosed behavior where Fable 5 silently degrades its own help on frontier-LLM-development requests, which Simon Willison flagged as quietly corrupting replies to slow rival research.

items.headline: CISA adds LiteLLM MCP command-injection flaw to KEV
items.diff_narrative: This advances the same MCP-as-most-exposed-surface throughline that 2026-06-09 carried as research - the VIPER-MCP scanner filing 67 CVEs, the NSA design-considerations guidance, and the unauthenticated Bleeding Llama Ollama memory-leak. Today that storyline crosses from research and disclosure into confirmed in-the-wild exploitation: CISA added CVE-2026-42271, a command-injection flaw in LiteLLM's unauthenticated MCP-server preview endpoints, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 9, following Horizon3.ai's chained-RCE confirmation. Chained with a Starlette host-header bypass it reaches CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE, and because LiteLLM brokers credentials for every connected provider, the abstract zero-trust agenda becomes a concrete, KEV-deadlined credential-theft path on the agent stack's tool-wiring layer.

items.headline: China drafts ~$295B AI-compute build with 80% domestic-hardware mandate
items.diff_narrative: A net-new state-policy event with no prior-day presence. China is preparing a roughly $295 billion, five-year program for a nationwide interconnected AI-data-center network with a mandate that at least 80% of the hardware come from domestic suppliers such as Huawei, Biren, and Moore Threads, explicitly walling off Nvidia and AMD. It hardens the US-versus-China compute-stack bifurcation as a concrete catalyst rather than a forecast, and reframes accelerator demand around a state-directed buyer underwriting a guaranteed home market for Chinese silicon.

items.headline: Broadcom-triggered chip drawdown deepens, AMD ~10% and Intel ~8% lower
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's chip-vendor share moves were attributed to Nvidia's entry into consumer laptop CPUs pressuring AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm on the day. Today the driver is different: a Broadcom-triggered semiconductor drawdown deepens, with AMD falling about 10% and Intel more than 8% in a single session on guidance contagion - Broadcom's $16B Q3 AI-chip guide undershot the ~$17.2B consensus and it declined to raise its full-year AI forecast - rather than any company-specific miss. The shift is that AI-capex sentiment is now being set at the margin by one hyperscaler-facing supplier's order book, re-rating the whole cohort together regardless of each name's own fundamentals.

items.headline: AI events to plan around: WWDC closes Friday, Databricks opens Monday
items.diff_narrative: The events calendar carries forward but the near-term anchors advance with the date. WWDC26 has moved from mid-week technical sessions to its Friday June 12 close, and the Databricks Data + AI Summit is now framed as opening Monday June 15 with this year's keynote and builder programming centered on Lakebase and MLflow (where yesterday cited only the 800-plus-session scale). The summer AI-security and AI-chip tracks are unchanged in substance - Confidential Computing Summit, AI Risk Summit, Black Hat, Hot Chips, AI Infra Summit - so the only standout movement is the dev-conference cluster ticking from upcoming to imminent.
